title: Democratic senators demand review of conditions on the USS Abraham Lincoln, other US warships participating in Iran blockade | CNN Politics
text:
Source: CNN

Two influential Democratic senators are demanding that the Pentagon investigate quality-of-life issues aboard Navy ships participating in the standoff with Iran, according to a letter shared exclusively with CNN.

Inthe lettersent Monday to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao, the lawmakers requested “an immediate independent strategic review” of the recent deployments of the USS Abraham Lincoln and USS Gerald R. Ford aircraft carriers and the USS Benfold destroyer, which spentfour days last month without powerin the South China Sea after an engineering failure.

The two carriers experienced extended deployments, with the well-being of crew members on the Lincoln gaining scrutiny earlier this month amidreports of difficult conditions.

The demand for an investigation came from the top Democrats on the Senate Appropriations Committee — Patty Murray of Washington, the committee vice chair, and Chris Coons of Delaware, who is also the top Democrat on the committee’s defense panel. The committee is considered powerful because it writes federal budget laws.

The requested independent review, the senators wrote, “should examine readiness issues related to operations, manning, quality of life, including mental health, and culture on the ships as well as communications with the crews’ families.” The senators asked that the review, if authorized, provide recommendations “to improve future extended deployments for sailors and Marines.”

The Ford recently completeda record-long deploymentthat included combat missions against Venezuela and Iran. The Lincoln is on its way home to San Diego to end a similarly long deployment that has featured virtually no shore time for sailors since a December 2025 stopover in Guam.

CNNpreviously reportedthat extended deployments beyond the Navy’s own seven-month target length have become increasingly common in recent years, with the median length of US-based aircraft carrier deployments steadily increasing since 2020.

Both the Ford and Lincoln experienced issues impacting their crew members, and the senators asked that the Navy detail plans to prevent similar issues in the future.

The Ford suffered amajor firethat started in the ship’s laundry department and required 30 hours to defeat, leading to roughly 600 sailors losing access to their bunks.

And CNN previously reported that sailors aboard the Lincoln experienced disruptions to the mail system and intermittent shortages of supplies such as hygiene items and fresh food.

Cao, inan August 14 statementon the Lincoln’s deployment, praised the crew’s endurance and argued that “our young men and women have been pushed to their limits — but they have never broken.”
